title: Constructibility and dimension bound for bad translate tuples
statement: Let $T$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], $p:H\to T$ a smooth separated group algebraic space of finite presentation, and $V\subseteq H$ a quasi-compact open subspace meeting every geometric fibre. Suppose every geometric fibre of $p$ is integral of the same dimension $d\geq0$. For algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], smoothness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; finite presentation also requires quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness, and separatedness means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. A group algebraic space is an algebraic space with multiplication, inverse and identity morphisms over its base satisfying the group identities, without a commutativity assumption. A geometric fibre is the base change to an algebraically closed field at a point of the base; integral means reduced, irreducible and nonempty. Give point spaces the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology], and use topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with the empty subset of dimension $-\infty$. For an integer $n\geq1$ put $X=H^{\times_T n}$. In $H\times_TX$ let $E_n$ be the closed subspace cut out by the conditions $g_j^{-1}x\notin V$ for $j=1,\ldots,n$, with the reduced induced closed structure. Let $Z_n\subseteq|X|$ be its image under projection. Then $Z_n$ is constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset]. For every geometric point $t:\operatorname{Spec}k\to T$, its inverse image in $|X_t|$ is exactly the set of tuples for which $H_t\ne\bigcup_jg_jV_t$, where this condition at any geometric tuple is tested after extending to an algebraically closed field containing its residue field. The Zariski closure of this inverse image in $|X_t|$ has dimension at most $nd-n+d$. The morphism $X\to T$ is smooth and separated of finite presentation with nonempty pure $nd$-dimensional geometric fibres. In particular, if $d=0$, then $E_n$ and $Z_n$ are empty.

source.place: Lemma 4.6, printed p.144: bad tuples Z, fibrewise codimension at least n-g. Incidence description: over an algebraically closed field, with C=H minus V, E_n has the same underlying closed set as H times C^n via (x,c_j) -> (x,g_j=x c_j^{-1}). Supporting constructibility: Stacks spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 0ECX (theorem-chevalley); product dimensions: varieties.tex Tag 0B2M (lemma-dimension-product-locally-algebraic), applied on etale charts. proof.text: Put $P_r=H^{\times_T r}$ for $r\geq1$ and $M=H\times_TX$. Induct on $r$: $P_1\to T$ is the given $p$, and $P_{r+1}\to P_r$ is the base change of $p$. Smoothness under base change and composition follows from [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus], applied to algebraic spaces viewed as discrete fibred groupoids. Separation and finite presentation follow in the same induction from [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality, lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. Thus $X\to T$ and $M\to T$ are smooth separated and of finite presentation. By [lem-sfb-space-fp-qcqs-source] they are qcqs, since the Noetherian scheme $T$ is qcqs. Their etale scheme charts are locally of finite type over $T$ (smoothness is tested on these charts), hence locally Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft]. In particular $X$ and $M$ are Noetherian algebraic spaces in the sense used by the Chevalley tool below.

source.place: Tags 03ZD, 03ZE, 03XR, 03KL, 03KQ, 03XQ, 06G5; Noetherianity on scheme charts uses Morphisms Tag 01T6.

proof.text: For each $j$ the morphism $a_j:M\to H$ is $(x,g_1,\ldots,g_n)\mapsto g_j^{-1}x$. Continuity of point maps [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] makes $F=\bigcap_j a_j^{-1}(|H|\setminus|V|)$ closed. By [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support] it has the reduced closed subspace $E_n$ specified in the statement. Its projection $q:E_n\to X$ is separated and of finite type: on every etale scheme chart it is a closed subscheme of $H\times_TX\to X$, so its coordinate algebras are quotients of finite-type algebras; it is quasi-compact since over an affine test the ambient base change is quasi-compact and its closed subset is quasi-compact. Its relative diagonal is the pullback of the closed relative diagonal of $H\times_TX\to X$ along $E_n\times_XE_n\to (H\times_TX)\times_X(H\times_TX)$, hence is closed [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-chevalley-image] to $q$ and the constructible subset $|E_n|$ of itself. Step 1 supplies its Noetherian target hypothesis, so $Z_n=q(|E_n|)$ is constructible.

proof.text:
Let $t:\operatorname{Spec}k	o T$ be geometric. The image/base-change equality of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] gives $Z_n	imes_{|X|}|X_t|=\operatorname{im}(|(E_n)_t|	o|X_t|)$, where the left side means inverse image. The support clause of [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support] says that a point of $(E_n)_t$ is exactly an incidence point satisfying all $g_j^{-1}x
otin V_t$; it does not assert that $(E_n)_t$ is reduced. Apply the same image/base-change equality at a tuple represented over an algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$ containing its residue field. Its membership is equivalent to the existence of a point of $H_\Omega$ outside every $g_jV_\Omega$, because $g_j^{-1}x
otin V_\Omega$ is exactly $x
otin g_jV_\Omega$. This is the asserted failure to cover. Nonemptiness is unchanged by extending the tuple field again, by the same point-surjectivity statement.

source.place: Tag 03H4 (lemma-points-cartesian); Tag 03IQ (lemma-reduced-closed-subspace), support after base change.

proof.text: Fix this geometric $t$ and write $G=H_t$. As the base change of $p$ along $t$, $G\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition] and of finite presentation [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], with group operations base changed from those of $H$. This separated finite-type group space $G/k$ is a separated scheme by [lem-sfb-locally-separated-group-space-scheme]: its closed diagonal is in particular an immersion. Its dimension is $d$ and it is integral by hypothesis. Let $C\hookrightarrow G$ be the reduced closed complement of the nonempty open $V_t$ [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support]. It is a finite-type $k$-scheme, since on affine charts its rings are quotients of the coordinate rings of $G$. Every strict chain of irreducible closed subsets of $C$ is also such a chain in $G$; appending the proper larger irreducible closed subset $G$ increases its length by one. Thus, by [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], if $C$ is nonempty then $d\geq1$ and $\dim C\leq d-1$. In particular $d=0$ forces $C$ empty. This chain argument needs no smoothness, properness, or commutativity.

source.place: Tags 08BH and 0B8F for schematic group spaces; dimension drop is the written chain argument from the definition, matching the incidence description in Deligne Lemma 4.6 (local PDF unavailable).

proof.text: On the scheme $G\times_kG^n$ consider the automorphism $\alpha(x,g_j)=(x,g_j^{-1}x)$ with inverse $\beta(x,c_j)=(x,xc_j^{-1})$. The two composites are the identity because $(xc_j^{-1})^{-1}x=c_j$ and $x(g_j^{-1}x)^{-1}=g_j$, without interchanging any factors. Under this automorphism the underlying closed support of $(E_n)_t$ becomes that of $G\times_kC^n$. The support/base-change assertion [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support] justifies this even though reduction need not commute with base change. Both $(E_n)_t$ and $G^n=X_t$ are schemes: the former is closed in the scheme $G\times_kG^n$. Homeomorphic spaces have the same Krull dimension [lem-weil-pbc-homeomorphism-krull-dimension]. If $C$ is empty, $n\geq1$ makes $(E_n)_t$ empty. Otherwise put $e=\dim C\leq d-1$ and induct on $r$ for $G\times_kC^r$, starting with $r=0$. The binary product formula [lem-sfb-scheme-product-dimension] gives dimension $d+re$ at each stage; [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] converts its local-ring dimension convention to topological dimension. Each value is nonnegative, so each successive product is nonempty, as required for the next application. Consequently $\dim(E_n)_t=d+ne\leq d+n(d-1)$. Apply [lem-zl-finite-type-fibre-image-dimension-bounds] to the $k$-morphism $(E_n)_t\to X_t$ between finite-type schemes. Its image is the inverse image of $Z_n$ by step 3, and hence the dimension of that image's closure is at most $d+n(d-1)=nd-n+d$. The empty case gives the same inequality with dimension $-\infty$.

source.place: Tag 0B2M (lemma-dimension-product-locally-algebraic), clause (2); Tag 0B2L (lemma-dimension-fibres-locally-algebraic), image-closure inequality; explicit incidence automorphism supplied by the agent.

proof.text: It remains to check purity of the tuple fibres, not just their global dimension. The integral finite-type scheme $G$ has one irreducible component of dimension $d$. Applying [lem-sbc-equidimensional-open-local-dimension] with $O=G$ gives $\dim_xG=d$ at every point. Smoothness of $G\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is inherited from $p$ by base change along $t$ [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus], and $G$ is a scheme by step 4, so it is smooth of relative dimension $d$ by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Inductively $G^r\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth of relative dimension $rd$: the case $r=1$ has just been checked; the projection $G^{r+1}\to G^r$ is a base change of $G\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, and composing this relative-dimension-$d$ map with the relative-dimension-$rd$ map proves the next case by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence]. Thus every point of $X_t=G^n$ has local topological dimension $nd$. It is locally Noetherian, being a finite-type scheme over a field [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft]. Apply [lem-sbc-constant-local-dimension-components] with $O=X_t$ to conclude that every irreducible component has dimension $nd$. The identity section supplies a point of $X_t$, so the fibre is nonempty. Together with step 1 this proves all the asserted properties of $X\to T$.

source.place: Tag 0A21 (lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic), parts (3),(5), and Morphisms Tags 02G1, 02G2 for fixed smooth relative dimension; the finite-product induction is written out.

proof.text: If $d=0$, step 4 makes $C$ empty on every geometric fibre, and step 5 makes every geometric fibre of $E_n\to T$ empty. If $E_n$ had a point, choose an algebraic closure of the residue field of its image in $T$. The point-surjectivity of the fibre-product map [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] would lift that point to this geometric fibre, a contradiction. Thus $E_n$ is empty and its image $Z_n$ is empty. This also covers an empty base $T$.
